claim_verbatim: On immigration, the new Congress is a lame duck before it sits. ICE’s $105.9 billion is already law, to 30 Sep 2029. Taking it back needs a law the President will veto, and Democrats can’t override. The deportation force is paid for past the next election.
context: X promotion of the 10 Nov essay 'Cold Civil War: The White House Against the House', which states the ICE money comes from Public Laws 119-21 and 119-98 and that 'A Democratic president elected in 2028 would inherit a deportation force already paid for.'
probability_words: will veto / can't override / is paid for (categorical, mapped as 'will')
resolution_criterion: YES (his call right) if, from 14 Nov 2026 to the 7 Nov 2028 presidential election, no enacted law rescinds, cancels, transfers away or bars obligation of 10% or more (about $10.6 billion) of ICE's $105.9 billion multi-year appropriation available to 30 Sep 2029 (Public Laws 119-21 and 119-98). NO if such a law is enacted in that window, whether signed or passed over a veto. A veto override of any ICE funding bill also counts as NO. The 10% threshold was set by the ledger, not by him.
